name: ID Stability
question: Is a pitcher's Spin ID stable enough to describe him?
data: Spin IDs as built with ID Schema v1 (frozen 2026-10-11) and the standard reference rule (four-seam if 100+, else sinker, else cutter), MLB regular seasons 2021-2026.
method: Uses each pitcher's standard Spin ID (ID Schema v1, frozen before this test was registered).
Year to year compares a pitcher's tilt offset in one season with the next, for pitchers who threw 300+ of the same reference fastball in both.
Odd vs. even games splits each qualifying season into alternating games and measures the tilt offset from each half the same way a full season is measured.
Slot changers are the year-to-year pairs whose arm slot moved 5° or more. If the offset is measured relative to the slot correctly, it should move much less than the slot did.
Each result has a 95% range from resampling pitchers 2,000 times. The pass or fail decision uses the measured value itself.

registered_metrics.sample: Every consecutive-season pair (2021-22 through 2025-26) for the same pitcher with the same reference type in both seasons and 300+ reference pitches in both. Pairs pooled; one point per pair.
registered_metrics.statistic: Pearson r between tilt offset in season N and season N+1

registered_metrics.description: Within-season split-half correlation (odd vs. even games)
registered_metrics.sample: Every pitcher-season (2021-2026) with 300+ reference pitches. The pitcher's games that season are ordered by date (then game ID) and split into odd- and even-numbered games. Each half needs 100+ reference pitches or the pitcher-season is left out.
registered_metrics.statistic: Pearson r between the two halves' tilt offsets, uncorrected (no Spearman-Brown). Each half is measured exactly like the season: quality-ok reference pitches, slot = mean arm angle, measured tilt = circular mean of pitch tilt, offset = frozen expected tilt for that slot minus measured, wrapped to -180..180.

registered_metrics.description: Slot changers: offset change vs. slot change
registered_metrics.sample: The year-to-year pairs above whose slot changed by 5 degrees or more.
registered_metrics.statistic: Median |offset change| divided by median |slot change|

gate_rule: The gate passes only if all three metrics pass. Decisions use the point estimates.
uncertainty: 95% intervals by bootstrap over pitchers (2,000 resamples, seed 11), reported alongside, not used to decide.

reported.description: Efficiency, year to year (same pairs; the efficiency value used in the ID)
Spin (Bauer units), year to year (same pairs)
Spin (Bauer units), odd vs. even games (same pitcher-seasons)
Efficiency, odd vs. even games: not computable (Baseball Savant publishes active spin per season only); reported as unavailable
reported.note: Not computable: Baseball Savant publishes active spin per season only.

conclusion: Passed. A pitcher's tilt offset holds up: one season predicts the next (r = 0.92, pass line ≥ 0.60), the two halves of a season agree (r = 0.99, pass line ≥ 0.80), and when the arm slot moves 5° or more, the offset moves 0.34 times as much as the slot (pass line ≤ 0.5). The Spin ID describes the pitcher, not one season's noise.
limitations: Only pitchers with 300+ reference pitches in both seasons count (mostly starters and busy relievers). Stability for low-volume arms isn't tested here.
Pitchers whose reference fastball changed between seasons (for example four-seam to sinker) are left out of the year-to-year pairs.
Odd and even games share a season's park, ball, and tracking calibration, so that check shows measurement consistency more than long-term stability.
The expected-tilt curve was fitted to 2023–2025, which overlaps the test seasons. It wasn't tuned for stability, but it isn't fully out of sample.
Efficiency comes from a season-level leaderboard, so its within-season stability can't be checked.
A correlation measures whether pitchers keep their order. Individual pitchers can still change; the slot-changer check looks at that directly.
